after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x
$$

the function is $f(x)={x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=2,$ and the upper bound is $b=6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{6-2}{n}=\frac{4}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+i\cdot \frac{4}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+\frac{4i}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{4i}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{4}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

What is ∫26x3dx expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?

a
 limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(2+4in)3⋅2n]
b
 limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(2+4in)3⋅4n]
c
 limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(4+2in)3⋅2n]
d
 limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(2+2in)3⋅2n]
e
 limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(4+in)3⋅1n]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1f(xi)⋅Δx,

where Δx=b−an and xi=a+iΔx.

In the definite integral,

∫26x3dx

the function is f(x)=x3, the lower bound is a=2, and the upper bound is b=6. So, we have

Δx=6−2n=4n,

and therefore

∫26x3dx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1f(xi)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[f(2+i⋅4n)⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[f(2+4in)⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[(2+4in)3⋅4n].

content.problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
content.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x
$$

the function is $f(x)={x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=2,$ and the upper bound is $b=6.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{6-2}{n}=\frac{4}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{6}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+i\cdot \frac{4}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(2+\frac{4i}{n})\cdot \frac{4}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{4i}{n})}^{3}\cdot \frac{4}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The shaded region lies under f(x)=x²−2x+2 and above the x-axis from x=0 to x=3. Since f(x)=(x−1)²+1 is positive, its area is the integral of f over [0,3].

For the function $f(x)={x}^{2}-2x+2$ shown above, what is the expression for the area $A$ as a definite integral?
after.worked_solution:
We want to express the area $A$ between the function $f(x)={x}^{2}-2x+2$ and the $x$-axis, between $x=0$ and $x=3.$

This can be expressed as the definite integral of $f(x)={x}^{2}-2x+2$ between the lower limit $x=0$ and the upper limit $x=3,$ as follows:

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{3}({x}^{2}-2x+2)\,\text{d}x
$$

after.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}9{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=9{x}^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=1$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-1}{n}=\frac{3}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}9{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(1+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(1+\frac{3i}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[9{(1+\frac{3i}{n})}^{\,3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
